item.title: Maya Joint reveals what Serena Williams did in their match at Wimbledon that ‘surprised’ her
item.description: Serena Williams made an incredible return to singles action at Wimbledon earlier this year. At the age of 44, Williams played her first singles match since 2022 on the grass courts of the All England Club. The American legend was pitted against Australian star Maya Joint, 24 years her junior, in the opening round of the tournament. Few were truly expecting Williams to be competitive after so long out of the sport, but the 23-time Grand Slam champion forced Joint to a decisive third set before coming up short 6-3, 6-7, 6-3. Photo by Tim Clayton/Getty Images Maya Joint reflects on her match with Serena Williams Reflecting on the match against Williams in an interview with Body and Soul , Joint said: “I was pretty nervous walking out onto that court knowing that everyone was going to cheer for her, but there were still plenty of people cheering for me, so that was nice. “Serena played better than I thought she was going to. Her movement was really good and that definitely took me a little bit by surprise.” Revealing what she said to Williams at the net after triumphing, Joint said: “I didn’t know what to say. “I panicked and just said, ‘Thank you.’ It was like, ‘Thank you for letting me breathe the same air that you breathe.’ I was just really relieved the match was over. That match was a turning point in the year. I started doing a lot better after that. “I think I got some confidence and relaxed a little bit, knowing that no match will be more difficult than that,” said Joint, who finished the 2026 season ranked 92nd in the world, having started the campaign ranked 32nd. Photo by Visionhaus/Getty Images Serena Williams results since her Wimbledon appearance Wimbledon marked the only tournament that Williams played singles at in 2026, though she continued featuring in doubles after her appearance in SW19. At the Cincinnati Open, Williams reunited with her sister Venus for the first time since the 2022 US Open. The Williams sisters, who claimed 14 Grand Slam titles and three Olympic gold medals as a duo in doubles, were competitive in Cincinnati, but ultimately lost to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in the opening round. Serena and Venus then teamed up at the US Open, but fell in the opening round once again. Serena also featured in Mixed Doubles at Flushing Meadows, partnering Carlos Alcaraz, and the two reached the quarterfinals.

item.title: Nashville SC's historic season is suddenly – and shockingly – on the ropes | Estes
item.description: Were this like most of the world’s soccer leagues, we’d have already had the parade down Broadway. But because this is the Americanized version of pro soccer, we do it our way. Major League Soccer’s regular season doesn’t decide the real champion. It's only as a prelude to a bracketed postseason that announces itself loudly, as in other North American sports, with hype videos and weighty slogans like “Leave no doubt.” That’s the phrase Nashville SC went with for its MLS Cup playoff run. Fitting, you’d concur, after such a magnificent and historic regular season. Nashville SC didn’t just have MLS’ best regular season in 2026. It had the best in league history, finishing with records in wins (23), points (77) and a meager three defeats (also a record) while claiming the Supporters’ Shield by a whopping 13-point margin (you guessed it: another record). But soccer, playoff form or not, is still going to be soccer. In a sport so fickle and unpredictable, goals are never guaranteed, and the better side often doesn't get one. No better explanation, really, for what just happened at Geodis Park on Nov. 22. For how Nashville SC, which hadn’t lost a home game to an MLS opponent all year, managed to lose a playoff opener 1-0 that it had no business losing. Nashville had already beaten FC Cincinnati twice in 2026 by a combined score of 6-0, and this, for the most part, was domination again in Game 1 of the best-of-three series. Nashville had possession for more than two-thirds of the game. It totaled 22 shots to Cincy’s five. Cincy, in fact, didn’t put a shot on goal until the 88th minute. The game’s lone goal was scored by a Nashville player. An errant pass by Patrick Yazbek got past Nashville goalkeeper Brian Schwake only seven minutes into the game. Cincy backed everyone in front of its goal and made the home team figure out a way through it. Little in sports is more tortuously frustrating as being a “better” soccer team having to chase a one-goal deficit against an underdog who was fortunate to get that goal, and therefore ceases advancing to try to score another, singularly focused on preventing an equalizer. “One of the most difficult things to do in the whole entire game is break down a low block,” Nashville defender Jack Maher said. “You see it in world football all the time, really.” Missed chances to score keep piling up. item.description: The OKC Blue were on the wrong side of a blowout in a 109-80 loss to the Austin Spurs on Sunday. The home defeat dropped their record to 2-5 in the G League 2026-27 regular season. Welp, this one lost any intrigue from the jump. The Blue were in a 37-25 hole after the first quarter. The offense fell apart in the second frame with just 18 points. That put them in a nasty 63-43 halftime deficit to the Spurs. The opening moments of the second half offered zero reassurance. The Spurs scored the first 10 points. That made it an eye-popping 73-43 score. The Blue only mustered 24 points in the third quarter. They were in an 89-67 deficit at that juncture of the game. The fourth quarter turned into garbage time as OKC only added 13 points. It trailed by as many as 33 points. Well, the only reason this was semi-watchable was Cason Wallace's appearance. Arm in a sling, he was in attendance to watch OKC's G League squad. The Thunder's 2026 NBA Cup court was still played on, funnily enough. The Blue shot 38% from the field and went 15-of-38 (39.5%) from 3. They shot 5-of-10 on free throws. They had 19 assists on 28 baskets. Five Blue players scored double-digit points. item.title: JJ Redick Addresses Luka Doncic’s Visible Frustration vs. Kings With A Reassuring Take On Leadership
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers recently defeated the Sacramento Kings 106-104 in a nail-biting NBA Cup fixture that they had hoped wouldn’t go down to the wire. In a viral halftime clip, Luka Doncic was caught on camera visibly frustrated with the Lakers’ lack of defensive effort, yelling at his teammates and coaches on the sideline. Days after the win, the Lakers’ head coach, JJ Redick, spoke to the media at the post-practice media scrum and addressed the incident while sharing his thoughts on Luka Doncic stepping into his leadership role. “I think what he’s been doing is great because he’s been leading, not out of frustration. Whether that moment was frustrating or not, f–k it was frustrating for me.” JJ Redick said . “It was a four-point game, and we didn’t execute the last shot. We turned a four-point game, which could have been tied if we executed correctly, into an eight-point game. I was steaming, and maybe that’s why I raised my voice a little bit at halftime.” “But he has been, whether it was that clip with Lindsey where he wanted to show something at a timeout, like, what I tell you guys all the time, that first minute is for the guys.” “And sometimes lately, I’ve been going over there early, just to sit, and I don’t say anything. Those guys have been awesome, and Luka is leading that. They are problem-solving in real time, and we encourage that, and those guys have been great together,” he concluded. Redick not only referred to the halftime incident at the Kings game, but also brought up the viral clip from the Suns game where Luka Doncic took the clipboard from the Lakers’ coaching staff after they almost threw away a 31-point lead that night. item.title: SEC fines Tennessee $250K after fans disrupted game vs. LSU by throwing golf balls and mustard
item.description: Tennessee has been fined $250,000 by the Southeastern Conference for fan conduct that disrupted Saturday's game against LSU, the conference announced Sunday. Fans at Neyland Stadium threw golf balls and mustard onto the field during the fourth quarter of the No. 9 Volunteers' win over Lane Kiffin's Tigers , leading the teams to stop play for a few minutes. In a statement, the SEC said the fine was assessed due to fans "throwing debris" onto the field, interrupting the game and "endangering contest participants." The SEC appeared to justify the fine with a bylaw referring to the availability of alcohol, saying that the conference can fine the school "if cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues." The SEC could also suspended the university's ability to sell alcohol at games, though it said it does not plan to do so at this time. The choice to throw golf balls and mustard was not by coincidence: The seemingly random combination is connected to the school's history with Kiffin. Tennessee's hatred of the LSU coach stems from Kiffin's brief stint as head coach of the Vols in 2009, before he left to coach USC after just one year. In 2021, Kiffin returned to Neyland Stadium for the first time, then coaching Ole Miss. He was greeted with Tennessee fans who threw random debris, including golf balls and a mustard bottle. At SEC media days, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel encouraged fans to reprise the moment when LSU came to Neyland. "I certainly hope our fan base hasn't cooled off," Heupel said at the time. "Whether it's the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they've got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival." A Tennessee field crew member carries a mustard bottle and golf balls off the field at Neyland Stadium. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Volunteers fans happily took on the challenge. In addition to bringing the items to throw at the LSU bench, several fans wore mustard bottles in the stands while cheering Tennessee to a 27-13 win. Kiffin, for what it's worth, took the situation in stride. "They listened to their coach," he said postgame. "I'm not being critical of him. I'm laughing at it."

item.title: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Canadiens land coveted center, but Red Wings get great haul from bad situation
item.description: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Canadiens land coveted center, but Red Wings get great haul from bad situation originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit is finally over — and he's going from one Original 6 teams to another. The former captain of the Red Wings, who demanded a trade back in June, is heading to the Montreal Canadiens , joining one of the NHL's youngest and most promising young cores. The deal comes after months of speculation as to where Larkin's next destination would be after he made clear his days as a Red Wing were over. Montreal was not rumored as one of Larkin's top destinations. As the owner of a no-trade clause, the 30-year-old center was trying to leverage his way to one of his top choices, which included the Minnesota Wild , the Vegas Golden Knights and the Florida Panthers . The Canadians were never viewed as a favorite to land him, but as one of the top teams in the Eastern Conference, he gets his wish, joining a club at the forefront of the Stanley Cup conversation. There is irony in the deal. Larkin's trade request came on the heels of a trend of American players asking out of their Canadian clubs, first Brady Tkachuk with the Ottawa Senators , and then Connor Hellebuyck with the Winnipeg Jets . The USA defeating Canada in the Olympic gold medal game in February undoubtedly played a role in those decisions. However, now Larkin finds himself doing the opposite — going from a struggling American club that hasn't made the playoffs since 2016 to one of the top Canadian markets. The Red Wings can put the drama behind them, and the Canadiens get a key piece to make a championship run this year and in years to come. But who is the real winner? The Sporting News hands out grades for the Larkin trade. The Habs have been looking for an upgrade at center behind captain Nick Suzuki. Larkin fits that role to a tee. With the Red Wings failing to make the playoffs during the Larkin era, it's become evident that he's not a true No. 1 center on a real contender. However, when it comes to being a second-line center, you'd be hard-pressed to find someone better in the league. Larkin has never been a point-per-game player, but he has been reliably in the 60-to-70 point range. He's far better suited in Montreal's top-six than Jake Evans or Kirby Dach, and gives the Habs one of the strongest 1-2 punches down the middle in the league. item.title: 49ers’ Nick Bosa jeered with ‘culero’ chants after Mexico City fan comments
item.description: MEXICO CITY — Nick Bosa came to Mexico with an idea about when the fans here ought to make noise. Sunday night, before the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings had played a down, the fans let him know they had a pretty good handle on the timing. They waited until Bosa stepped onto the field for warmups at Estadio Banorte, better known as Estadio Azteca. Then came the boos, whistles and chants of “¡Culero!” — roughly “a–hole” in Mexican Spanish. He heard more of the same once the game got underway. Bosa had wanted the crowd to pick its spots. It picked one. Nick Bosa #97 of the San Francisco 49ers hits Kirk Cousins #8 of the Minnesota Vikings as he throws a pass in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. Getty Images For a guy who plays for what felt like Mexico City’s favorite team Sunday night, that took some doing. Bosa managed it earlier in the week when he got to talking about the crowd at the 49ers’ last game here, in 2022. What the San Francisco defensive end remembered was the chanting. What he wanted this time was a little help for the home team, or at least the team that figured to feel most at home. Fair enough. Then he kept talking. “Yeah, I kind of want, I think we need some information given to the fans, so they know when to cheer,” Bosa said. “Because they just chant the whole time. If we can kind of teach them, no offense to them and their soccer cheering techniques, but if they can cheer when we’re on defense, that would be great.” Fans cheer during the first half of an NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There’s a good football point in there. Get loud enough when the Vikings have the ball and it gets harder for their offensive linemen to hear the snap count. Ask any 49ers fan in Santa Clara to lend Bosa a hand with that and odds are they’d be happy to oblige. It was the offer to teach that got him in trouble. American football has been played in Mexico for years. In fact, Mexico City fans were packing Estadio Azteca for NFL games before Bosa was born. In 1994, 112,376 showed up to watch the Cowboys play the Houston Oilers – in the preseason. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins throws a pass against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Eduardo Verdugo In 2005, another 103,467 turned out to see Bosa’s own 49ers face the Cardinals in the first NFL regular-season game played outside the United States. The league puts its Mexican fan base at 40 million nationwide, its largest outside the U.S. That’s the crowd Bosa offered to teach when to cheer. You can imagine how the folks who grew up watching it here felt about a visiting player offering pointers on how to root for a team plenty of them have loved longer than he’s played for it. item.description: Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images Jaguars’ Liam Coen explains thought process behind controversial late-game FG decision in Giants loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Coach Liam Coen ’s Jacksonville Jaguars fell to 7-3 after a 23-18 road loss to the New York Giants that included a controversial late-game decision to kick a field goal and the loss of a key defender to a chest injury . Running back Bhayshul Tuten got an injury downgrade before the game, but played through it as the Jaguars’ rushing attack struggled in a tough loss. Afterward, Coen explained why he decided to kick a field goal with 3:43 to go on the clock, as shared by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network. He said he and his coaching staff talked about possibly going for it, but the charts told him to kick the field goal. Pochettino is set to leave the U.S. national team to become head coach of Manchester United following the November international window. Mandatory Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images Mauricio Pochettino’s first match as Manchester United manager ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday, leaving the club still rooted near the bottom of the Premier League. United entered the game in 18th place after one win in their first 10 league matches—their worst start in 40 years. Michael Carrick had been sacked earlier in the month, and Pochettino was appointed on a deal through 2029 after finishing his duties with the U.S. national team. He arrived in Manchester only days earlier, vowing to rebuild “from scratch” and restore confidence. The Anfield debut unraveled quickly. Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute for a foul on Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free kick, and Florian Wirtz added a second minutes later. Liverpool controlled the rest of the match, with further goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz completing the rout. United never recovered from the early numerical disadvantage. This is kinda what it looked like… Liverpool against Manchester united Highlights pic.twitter.com/0seVpMCaDY — Troll Foot (@troll__foot) November 22, 2026 Pochettino later defended his players’ effort and rejected talk of immediate relegation, noting that the red card made the task nearly impossible. The result matched the joint-heaviest opening defeat for a United manager in the modern era. Fans at Anfield taunted the new coach with “sacked in the morning” chants barely two weeks into his tenure. The Argentine inherits a squad short on confidence and identity after years of inconsistency since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement. His high-pressing, attacking principles will take time to implement. Upcoming fixtures against Sporting in the Champions League and Brentford at home offer little respite. For now, the Pochettino era at Old Trafford is defined by the same problems that prompted his appointment: a side struggling to compete, now with a new voice but the same urgent need for results. item.description: A season filled with upset wins for the Rutgers men’s soccer team ended in heartbreaking, ironic fashion: with the Scarlet Knights being on the wrong end of a surprise result. The third-seeded Scarlet Knights suffered a 2-1 loss to six-seed Cornell in the second round of the NCAA Tournament on Sunday in Piscataway, conceding a golden goal in extra time that ended their 2026 season with a crushing loss. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. Efforts to build a complex in Baltimore for an MLS Next Pro operation have floundered. (Meanwhile, United's owners have launched a pro volleyball team.)
